content: 1. Refer the woman for family planning counseling to discuss contraceptive options and birth spacing. 2. Dispense a three-month supply of iron supplements and provide counseling on the importance of adherence to the treatment regimen. 3. Administer any due treatments or prophylaxis, such as tetanus immunization, if the woman has not completed the full course. 4. Encourage the use of insecticide-treated bed nets to protect both the mother and baby from mosquito-borne diseases. 5. Record all findings and treatments in the mother’s home-based maternal record for continuity of care. 6. Advise the woman to return to the health center for a follow-up visit six weeks after childbirth. 7. Counsel the woman to avoid tobacco, alcohol, and drug use, and to minimize exposure to second-hand smoke. 8. If severe hypertension is present, administer appropriate antihypertensive medication and urgently refer the woman to a hospital. 9. For moderate hypertension, reassess in one week, and if the condition persists, refer the woman to a hospital. 10. If blood pressure is normal, no additional treatment is required. 11. If pallor is observed, assess for anemia by checking for a history of bleeding, measuring hemoglobin levels, and examining for conjunctival or palmar pallor. 12. In cases of severe anemia, provide a double dose of iron (60 mg twice daily for three months), urgently refer to a hospital, and follow up in two weeks to monitor progress and adherence. 13. For moderate anemia, provide a double dose of iron for three months and reassess at the next postnatal visit in four weeks. If anemia persists, refer to a hospital. 14. If no anemia is detected, continue iron supplementation for a total of three months. 15. Check the woman’s HIV status if not previously tested or if her status is unknown. Provide counseling on the importance of knowing her HIV status, the benefits of testing, and confidentiality of results. 16. If the woman is HIV-positive, refer her and her baby to HIV services for further assessment, counsel on infant feeding options, and provide additional care, including family planning and safer sex practices. 17. If the HIV test is negative, counsel on maintaining a negative status through safer sex practices, including condom use. 18. If the woman refuses HIV testing or her status is unknown, counsel on safer sex practices and the importance of partner testing. 19. If heavy or light vaginal bleeding persists six weeks postpartum, refer the woman to a hospital. 20. If fever or foul-smelling lochia is present, assess for uterine infection by checking for heavy bleeding, abnormal lochia, and abdominal tenderness. Administer IV fluids and antibiotics as needed, and urgently refer to a hospital. 21. For upper urinary tract infections, administer appropriate IM/IV antibiotics and urgently refer to a hospital. 22. For lower urinary tract infections, provide oral antibiotics, encourage increased fluid intake, and follow up in two days. If no improvement, refer to a hospital. 23. If very severe febrile disease is suspected, insert an IV line, administer appropriate antibiotics and antimalarial treatment, and urgently refer to a hospital. 24. For malaria, provide oral antimalarial medication and follow up in two days. If no improvement, refer to a hospital. 25. If urinary incontinence is present, check for perineal trauma and provide oral antibiotics if a lower urinary tract infection is suspected. If the condition persists for more than one week, refer to a hospital. 26. For perineal trauma with signs of infection, such as pus, refer the woman to a hospital. 27. For perineal pain or infection, remove sutures if present, clean the wound, counsel on hygiene, provide paracetamol for pain, and follow up in two days. If no improvement, refer to a hospital. 28. If the woman reports feeling unhappy or crying easily, assess for postpartum depression by asking about mood, energy levels, sleep, and enjoyment of usual activities. Provide emotional support and refer urgently to a hospital if postpartum depression is suspected. 29. For postpartum blues, reassure the woman that this is common, listen to her concerns, provide emotional support, and counsel her partner and family to assist her. Follow up in two weeks and refer if no improvement. 30. If abnormal vaginal discharge is present four weeks postpartum, assess for itching, partner urinary problems, and abnormal discharge characteristics (amount, color, odor). Treat for possible infections such as gonorrhea, chlamydia, candida, or bacterial infections with appropriate antibiotics or antifungal medication. Counsel on safer sex practices and refer to a hospital if no improvement. 31. If the woman has a cough or difficulty breathing, assess the duration, presence of chest pain, blood in sputum, and signs of breathlessness or wheezing. 32. For possible pneumonia, administer the first dose of IM/IV antibiotics and urgently refer to a hospital. 33. For chronic lung disease, refer to a hospital for assessment and counsel on smoking cessation if applicable. 34. For upper respiratory tract infections, advise on safe remedies, counsel on smoking cessation, and avoid exposure to second-hand smoke. 35. If the woman is taking anti-tuberculosis drugs, reassure her that the medication is safe for her baby and emphasize the importance of completing treatment. Plan for INH prophylaxis for the newborn if the mother’s sputum is TB-positive within two months of delivery. 36. If signs suggest severe or advanced symptomatic HIV infection, assess for weight loss, diarrhea, fever, cough, difficulty breathing, and other symptoms. Refer to a hospital for further assessment. 37. Counsel on stopping tobacco, alcohol, and drug use, and refer to specialized care providers if substance abuse is present. 38. For postpartum care, always begin with a rapid assessment and management approach, followed by a thorough postpartum examination. Record all findings and treatments in the home-based and clinic records. 39. Advise the woman and her family on postpartum care, hygiene, nutrition, and when to seek medical attention. Reinforce counseling on safer sexual practices and the importance of family planning. 40. Promote the use of impregnated bed nets for the mother and baby to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. 41. Ensure the woman knows when to return for her next health facility visit. 42. Provide tetanus immunization if the woman has not completed the full course. 43. Dispense a three-month supply of iron supplements and counsel on adherence to the treatment regimen. 44. Record all findings and treatments in the mother’s home-based maternal record. 45. Advise the woman to avoid tobacco, alcohol, and drug use, and to minimize exposure to second-hand smoke.
